summary: B1 Explore review completed with changes-requested. The proposed B1 scope, state schemas, terminal immutability, outputs boundary, Archify restraint, and fixture-oriented test strategy are generally aligned. Two blocking contract conflicts remain: the Explore treats a reference-only `change-checkpoint` entry as part of the fixed Action Catalog despite the frozen core-model catalog being exhaustive without it, and it hard-codes ResultRef to a Run-path representation even though the frozen integration boundary requires a provider-neutral logical reference. The Explore must reconcile these before B1 can create a Proposal.

blockingFindings.title: The proposed fixed Action Catalog conflicts with the frozen core-model contract
blockingFindings.evidence: The Explore requires CHANGE_ACTIONS to contain eleven entries including change-checkpoint. The frozen core-model Requirement states that the fixed main Actions are explore, propose, apply, archive and that its auxiliary Actions are the six listed review/revise actions; it does not include change-checkpoint. The implementation reference section 6.3 does include it. The Explore selects the reference's interpretation without recording or resolving the contradiction between the frozen sources.
blockingFindings.impact: An implementation cannot demonstrate exact conformance to both frozen Action Catalog definitions. Treating the reference as silently overriding the formal product spec would create a second, undocumented catalog authority and can mislead later Policy implementation.
blockingFindings.requiredResolution: Revise the Explore to explicitly resolve this source conflict before Proposal. Either preserve the core-model catalog exactly and model Change Checkpoint only as the required Git boundary, or obtain and record an authorized contract change that adds change-checkpoint to the core-model catalog. The resulting catalog, rationale, and acceptance tests must have one authoritative definition; do not silently choose between the sources.

blockingFindings.title: ResultRef is prematurely fixed to a Run-path transport format
blockingFindings.evidence: Q9 defines ResultRef as required runPath and sha256 fields. The frozen integration boundary defines ResultRef as a logical, provider-neutral reference that may map to a Git revision, Run result, artifact version, content hash, or another unambiguous version reference. It assigns the Action Package/Result/ResultRef logical boundary to C1.
blockingFindings.impact: Mandatory runPath excludes legitimate Git- or artifact-backed results and couples the domain type to one filesystem layout before C1 defines the adapter/schema boundary. Later Review and continuation logic would not be able to represent all formally supported result sources without breaking B1's public type.
blockingFindings.requiredResolution: Keep B1's type boundary provider-neutral and defer the concrete serialized ResultRef schema/adapter mapping to C1. At minimum, remove mandatory runPath and describe the type in terms of stable identity, version/change detection, and optional locator capabilities that can represent the allowed reference kinds. Carry that boundary into the Proposal and tests.
